requirements.description: Fellowships are provided to excellent researchers undertaking international mobility.
Applications are made jointly by the researcher and a beneficiary in the academic or non-academic sector.

Postdoctoral Fellowships take place either in Europe (an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country) as a European Fellowship, or in a Third Country not associated to Horizon Europe as a Global Fellowship.
European Postdoctoral Fellowships must have a standard duration between 12 and 24 months.
Global Postdoctoral Fellowships require a 12-24 month outgoing phase in a non-associated Third Country and a mandatory 12-month return phase to an EU Member State or Associated Country host.

A secondment phase may optionally be included within the overall duration of the fellowship in any country worldwide (European PF: not exceeding half the requested duration; Global PF: up to half of the outgoing phase); it must add significant value and align with project objectives.

An optional non-academic placement of up to six months at the end of the project may be requested at a non-academic host in an EU Member State or Associated Country; if requested, the placement must be an integral part of the proposal and meet the sectoral and geographic requirements.
Training activities must integrate key transferable skills including digital ones (e.g. generative AI) and foster Open Science, knowledge valorisation, and research integrity.
A Career Development Plan must be established jointly by the supervisor(s) and the researcher and submitted as a deliverable at the beginning of the action.
Specific eligibility conditions apply to fellowships in the research areas covered by the Euratom Research and Training Programme; this scope element applies only to Euratom-covered research.
ERA Fellowships (implemented through Work Programme Annex 11) provide specific support for undertaking the fellowship in a widening country; this is an optional pathway.
